generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: Copy an existing parent primary-key value; never NULL (FK column is NOT NULL by PK role).
generic_sampling_rules.real_score: Uniform real in [8.5, 10.0] rounded to 3 decimals.
generic_sampling_rules.real_total: Uniform real in [50.0, 60.0] rounded to 3 decimals; no sum formula asserted.
generic_sampling_rules.real_age: Integer-valued real drawn from {15..40}, weighted toward 19-24.
generic_sampling_rules.real_height: Uniform real in [1.55, 2.05] rounded to 2 decimals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Draw from a pool of realistic full names of 10-17 entries; allow accented/unaccented and case variants at ~15% share so 20-50% of rows share a name with another row.
generic_sampling_rules.text_place: Draw from a small pool of 6 city names; include 'Santo Domingo' and variant 'santo domingo'; allow case variants at ~10% share.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_numeric: For each listed literal L, generate values L-step, L, L+step where step is the column's rounding step (0.001 scores, 0.01 measures, 1 for ages).
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates_for_distinct: Ensure 20-50% of rows share a value with another row on the targeted column via pool reuse.
generic_sampling_rules.ties_for_order: Ensure at least two rows share the same value on the ORDER column.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: Schema DDL declares no NOT NULL constraints and observed null_rate is 0.0; therefore plant no NULLs in any non-PK column. All non-PK columns are sampled with non-NULL values only. This is stated explicitly to resolve the nullable-mismatch: the compact DB has zero NULLs and the generator matches that.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_value_share: For text pools, ~80% of draws reuse a pool value (producing duplicates); ~20% are fresh on first appearance.

targets.rule: Generate people rows (n_people >= 8) and gymnast rows with n_gym <= n_people - 2; sample gymnast.Gymnast_ID without replacement from people.People_ID, guaranteeing at least 2 parent rows without children. No NULL FK (Gymnast_ID is PK).

Hometown: deterministically assign group sizes {0,1,2,3} across four distinct pool values (one pool value absent -> size 0, one appears once, one twice, one three times; remaining rows fill other pool values, at least one more pool value present twice elsewhere). Gymnast_ID: unique per person and PK; within a group of people by Hometown, COUNT(DISTINCT gymnast_id) can be 0 (no gymnast row), 1, 2, or 3 depending on how many of the group's people have gymnast rows; construction guarantees each of those group sizes exists for COUNT(DISTINCT) over the join. COUNT(*) over Hometown groups covers 0/1/2/3.

Hometown: 20-50% duplicate share via group-size construction (see aggregate_boundary). Name: 20-50% duplicate share via pool reuse; include at least 3 name values each appearing twice. Gymnast_ID: unique PK, no duplicates; distinct-count variation arises only via join multiplicity.

Hometown must include 'Santo Domingo' and the case variant 'santo domingo' in every instance (deterministic assignment, not probabilistic). Age: force at least one row each at ages 19, 20, 21, 22 so predicates age < 19/20/21/22 separate.
Intentionally unsatisfiable: People_ID is a unique PK so ORDER BY People_ID ASC has no ties at any rank. No construction required; no duplicate PKs may be introduced.

Apply after all other height assignment and after any null rule (no nulls planted anyway): with n_people >= 3, set heights[0] = heights[1] = max(heights) and ensure at least one other row has a strictly smaller height, so MAX(height) matches >= 2 rows and >= 2 distinct heights exist. Guard: only force when n_people >= 3.
Include at least one row each with Total_Points = 57.4, 57.5, 57.6 (the literal boundary 57.5 and one step either side); remaining rows drawn from [50.0, 60.0].

semantic_rules_and_formulas.formula: Hometown IN ('Santo Domingo','santo domingo','Bonao','Miami','Santiago de los Caballeros','La Romana','Los Alcarrizos')

semantic_rules_and_formulas.evidence: Observed Total_Points 57.374-58.061; range narrowed from [0,60] toward observed band. Sum formula dropped: row 4 (8.987+9.75+9.75+9.762+9.787+9.725=57.761 vs observed 57.649) contradicts it.

supporting_evidence.Total_Points_formula: Sum formula checked on rows 1 (58.061), 2 (57.924) and dropped on row 4 (57.761 vs 57.649); not asserted. Range rule uses observed min/max 57.374/58.061 with bound [50,60].
supporting_evidence.score_ranges: All six apparatus scores observed in [8.987, 9.787]; real_score uses [8.5, 10.0].
supporting_evidence.null_policy: DDL has no NOT NULL; observed null_rate 0.0 for every column; generator plants no NULLs and null_targets is empty. This explicitly resolves the engineer's nullable-mismatch by choosing option (b): restrict NULL planting to spec-marked columns (none).

uncertainty: Total_Points does not equal the sum of the six apparatus scores on all shown rows (row 4 mismatch), so no sum formula is asserted. Hometown group sizes {0,1,2,3} and Gymnast_ID distinct-counts are constructed deterministically given n_people=10, n_gym=7; if the size selector varies sizes, keep n_gym <= n_people - 2 and n_people >= 8 to preserve unmatched_join_rows and the size-3 Hometown group.
